pageCache.pageTitle: Home - St Helen's Catholic Primary School, Chargeable Lane, London, E13 8DW
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome and thank you for taking the time to visit our school website. St Helen’s is a happy, family-like environment where each child can flourish spiritually, socially, and academically. We recognise the gifts of each child and nurture them to achieve their full potential. Our strong focus, centred around Christ; living out the Gospel values and Catholic Social Teachings is at the heart of all that we do.
Learning at St Helen’s is fun, safe, and enriched every day; we fully promote learning at school and at home, recognising the important role of working in partnership with parents and the community. Celebrating the diversity of the community and our families makes St Helen’s a wonderful place where everybody can grow together.Three generations of my family, including myself, attended St Helen’s as children and so I view my journey from child, to teacher, to senior leader and into my headship here as an incredible testament to the school. My vision is to have similarly high expectations for all our children too.
I hope that this website provides an insight into what life is like at St Helen’s. Please click to see St Helen's creative film.With best wishes,​Miss Claire DohertyHeadteacher​

Remembrance Day-Peace
To celebrate Remembrance day we held our own remembrance service in school where we observed the 2 minutes silence and prayed for all those who have been affected by war. Our Student council went to East Ham cenotaph and were joined by other local schools where they represented the whole of St Helens and participated in a small service to honour the day.

pageCache.pageTitle: Celebrating 150 Years of St Margaret’s Parish - St Helen's Catholic Primary School, Chargeable Lane, London, E13 8DW
pageCache.text:
Celebrating 150 Years of St Margaret’s Parish
Celebrating 150 Years of St Margaret’s ParishThe pupils and staff of St Helen’s Catholic Primary School were truly privileged to be part of a very special celebration as our parish, St Margaret’s, marked its 150th anniversary. In a wonderful gathering of faith and community, Holy Mass was celebrated in the grounds of our very own school, in the company of Bishop Alan. It was a spectacular and deeply memorable occasion for our whole community.Our pupils were honoured to take part in the celebration by reading the Bidding Prayers, giving thanks for the wonderful parish community that has been built and nurtured over 150 years. Their prayers reflected the strength, love and togetherness that continues to unite our parish and school families.Music was also at the heart of this special celebration. Our St Helen’s School Choir joined the Parish Choir, sharing the Word of God through beautiful hymns. Some of the hymns had been chosen by our children, while others were selected by Father John and our parishioners, bringing together the voices and traditions of both our school and parish.St Helen’s feels truly blessed to be part of such a close knit and welcoming Catholic community, working together for the common good and living out our Gospel values through faith, service and love for one another.The celebration was a beautiful reflection of our shared journey — bringing together old faces, new faces and generations of families, while looking forward to the continued growth and building of our community. We give thanks for the past 150 years of St Margaret’s Parish and feel blessed to be part of its story as we continue to walk together in faith.Happy 150th Anniversary, St Margaret’s!

pageCache.pageTitle: Religious Education - St Helen's Catholic Primary School, Chargeable Lane, London, E13 8DW
pageCache.text:
Religious Education
The intent behind the curriculum for Religious Education is to develop young people to become religiously literate, to have the knowledge, understanding and skills – appropriate to their age and capacity - to think spiritually, ethically and theologically and to be aware of the demands of religious commitment in everyday life. To create opportunities to develop and promote the school’s community spirit, ethos and Gospel values.
Leaders ensure that the Catholic life of the school is at the root of every learning opportunity provided. The curriculum is reviewed annually to ensure the intent is current with the demands the children may be facing in society addressing the principles of Catholic Social teaching. The leader envisions children making the right choices, through learning about their faith and the scripture. In turn they will help the wider community, spreading the Good News of Jesus.
Personal, social, health and Citizenship education (PSHCE) enables our children tobecome healthy, independent and responsible members of a society. It aims tohelp them understand how they are developing personally and socially, andtackles many of the moral, social and cultural issues that are part of growing up.We provide our children with opportunities for them to learn about rights andresponsibilities and appreciate what it means to be a member of a diverse society.Our children are encouraged to develop their sense of self-worth by playing apositive role in contributing to school life, the wider community and globally.

pageCache.text:
The Parishioners Christmas Lunch
Each year St Helen’s looks forward to hosting the over 50’s parishioners Christmas lunch. Working with the parish priests of St Margaret’s the staff at St Helen’s volunteer to prepare and serve a full Christmas dinner to those that attend. It is a day of fun as the parishioners enjoy a meal, games and music as well as having time to talk with friends and members of the local community.

pageCache.text:
Year 5 Pilgrimage to Aylesford - Participation
To kick start our year the year 5’s went on a pilgrimage to Aylesford where they learned about the historical site and deepened their faith. During this Pilgrimage the children learned about the main shrine, chapels and the rosary garden. The also took some reflection time while praying the rosary and spent time with God at the main shrine. We then ended the day with a Mass to give thanks with St Joachim’s led by Father Dan it was a wonderful way to start off our year.
